scope: The positive-integer minimum in Eq. (1) exists for every real time and positive tolerance.

Factorial and geometric inequalities convert any qualifying positive cutoff Q at tolerance at most one into a degree 16Q Taylor truncation with remainder at most ε²/6750. These constants serve the cubic amplification proof.

The local construction encodes the sine and cosine Taylor polynomials with common attenuation sin(π/54). Repeated cubic amplification preserves the two signal flags, multiplies the ideal angle by three and increases the compression error by at most 15 per level.

For a Hermitian contraction given by a same-frame projected unitary encoding, the finite two-flag circuit makes 27(64Q+1) controlled encoding queries at the least Eq. (1) cutoff. It attains spectral compression error ε²/2, clean state-vector error ε and postselection probability at least 1−ε². The fixed-gate ledger counts matrix instructions.
The local word calculus tracks products, inverses, oracle-free gates and substitution. A separate counter records each physical query label. These are implementation lemmas for the compiled circuit.
Controlling a unitary compute–act–uncompute sandwich needs only the middle operation controlled. The computation and its inverse act on the original register, with both signal flags untouched.

The fixed instructions in the compiled signal polynomial and its amplified word are conjugate-paired fiber phases, flag operations, cubic phases ±i about the signal frame, or adjoints of those instructions.

For every finite standard-form input H=⟨0|G†UG|0⟩ at 0<ε<1, a single oracle-independent word attains spectral error ε²/2 and success probability at least 1−ε². Its two signal flags suffice. The exact ledgers are 54(64Q+1) ordinary G queries and 27(64Q+1) controlled U queries including inverses. The fixed-gate count is at the level of matrix instructions.
Finite-register calculations for Lemma 6 verify the clean coordinate frame, uniform slot amplitudes, reversible permutations, norm-bounded decoder rotations and the encoded matrix entries.

The row-slot permutation, XOR lookup, public decoder rotation and swap give a projected unitary encoding of the normalized sparse Hermitian matrix. Its controlled implementation makes exactly two ordinary row-position queries and two ordinary binary-value queries.

Lemma 6 for exact finite binary encodings. For any positive entry scale b, the two sparse oracles of Eq. (11) yield a clean-coordinate encoding of H/(db) using two queries to each oracle. A row permutation extends each position map beyond its d designated slots. Taking b to be the maximum entry norm gives the published normalization for every nonzero input.

For an exact m-bit normalized entry code, a fixed decoder and d row slots, the simulation at physical time t uses 54(64Q+1) ordinary calls to each of the position and value oracles, with Q evaluated at tdb. Its compressed operator error is at most ε²/2 and its Born success probability is at least 1−ε². The theorem counts oracle calls.
The two averaging flags can be prepared by single-qubit Hadamards up to a common unit phase. The designated coordinate projector and the unitary change of frame are explicit.
A conjugate-paired fiber phase is an ancilla test, a two-flag phase and the inverse test. The two cubic phases are globally phased coordinate reflections conjugated by Hadamards.

These coordinate identities realize the fixed unitaries on the two signal flags. A CNOT has a single negative eigenvector, allowing a fixed two-flag basis change to produce the selective sign in cubic amplification.

The emitted, addressed Clifford+T words perform the exact ancilla-coordinate toggles on every basis input. The single-flag test borrows the other flag, and the two-flag test borrows one physical system wire. Reversible bit complements select the desired ancilla coordinate.

These word-construction lemmas compile the fixed operators into legal one- or two-wire gates, compose and invert the expansions and preserve the per-oracle ledger and execution semantics through substitution.

Theorem 1 specialized to an a-qubit ancilla and an r-qubit system with r ≥ 1. The uniform simulation uses a+r+2 wires, 54(64Q+1) preparation-oracle calls, 27(64Q+1) controlled block queries and at most 250(a+4)(27(64Q+8)−2) additional one- or two-qubit gates. Spectral error is at most ε²/2 and success is at least 1−ε² at the least Eq. (1) cutoff.

Binary coordinate inclusion preserves inner products. Extending a matrix by identity on unused basis coordinates preserves unitarity and Hermiticity, respects products, and intertwines the matrix exponential. Padding the preparation and block oracles produces the padded logical Hamiltonian.

For any d-dimensional ancilla and any finite logical system of dimension N ≥ 2, including non-powers of two, the padded physical oracle simulation uses ⌈log₂ d⌉ + ⌈log₂ N⌉ + 2 qubits and a counted one- and two-wire gate list. Spectral error and success are proved for the original encoded inputs.

The computational coordinate frame is isometric. Conjugating the word by the two-flag Hadamard changes its preparation and postselection basis while preserving the compressed matrix and every Born success probability.

Theorem 1 for any finite d ≥ 1 and N ≥ 2. The least Eq. (1) cutoff controls the preparation and block query counts. There are at most 250(⌈log₂ d⌉+4)(27(64Q+8)−2)+2 individually verified one- and two-qubit gates, including flag preparation and computational-basis readout, on the exact ceiling-log register widths. Spectral error is at most ε²/2 and success at least 1−ε².
Three Toffoli gates and two single-qubit flips implement one full-adder carry for a strict comparison. Fresh wire addresses keep the inputs and other carries intact.

A most-significant-first pair of p-bit quantum inputs can be compared by a reversible circuit of at most 47p addressed one- and two-qubit gates. A clean seed and clean carries yield the numerical strict less-than bit. The emitted word also has an exact action on initially dirty carries.

The mean of the ±1 less-than phase over a uniform p-bit word is the offset-binary fixed-point input value. The forward reversible threshold comparator, a one-wire phase and the inverse comparator realize this phase coherently.

Replacing selected wire values gives a bijection to a Boolean register while keeping all other wires fixed. A p-gate addressed Hadamard word gives the exact uniform mean of a diagonal phase in a clean diagonal matrix element.
The sparse-entry decoder routes its two numerical comparators across distinct data, carry, seed and component-selector wires. The comparators preserve the real/imaginary selector.

These implementation lemmas check unitarity and primitive-gate counts, preserve the untouched threshold and carry inputs under the random-bit preparation, and establish the selected comparison phase for both Cartesian components.

One fixed unitary reads two p-bit offset-binary Cartesian coordinates and encodes (x+iy)/2 exactly as its diagonal amplitude with workspace initialized to zero. The circuit uses at most 190p+4 addressed one- or two-qubit gates on 5p+3 wires. This is the binary-value decoder layer for the sparse simulation proof.
Unitary operator norms and compression by isometries bound the norm of the projected signal.
Embedding each input vector at a fixed computational ancilla value preserves its norm.
A finite normalized nonnegative amplitude table extends to a unitary with that table as its designated column. This is an existence and matrix identity used for uniform slot preparation.
A selector made of unitary diagonal blocks is unitary.
The block-encoding compression error supplies a squared-amplitude lower bound on successful postselection of a normalized input.
The range of a coordinate-fiber isometry is exactly its computational-basis projector.
Cubic coherent amplification is implemented by an expanded query word with an explicit compressed-matrix identity and resource ledger.
Cubic signal amplification triples the ideal angle, obeys a perturbation estimate, and converts compressed operator approximation to a clean-frame vector guarantee.
Parallel direct sums of oracle matrices preserve products, identity, adjoints and unitarity.

Hermitian projected encodings implement the real polynomial response, accept a scalar phase and combine the sine/cosine Taylor polynomials to form the complex exponential truncation.
Averaging two compatible block encodings preserves isometric frames and yields their mean as the encoded operator.

An addressed Hadamard word on zero bits has the exact uniform column on those coordinates. Counting words below a threshold gives the threshold as a complex-valued sum.
Unitary Hamiltonian evolution preserves normalization. Hadamard and Pauli X are unitary, and involutive basis permutations are unitary and self-adjoint.
Tensor gates multiply componentwise, preserve identities and act unitarily for unitary factors.
